caption: The drawing depicts a six-sided lantern with a slightly tapered, hexagonal shape, rendered in a realistic style. The frame of the lantern is brown and appears to be made of metal, with visible edges and joints at each corner. The panels of the lantern are transparent, likely representing glass, and each side is bordered by the brown frame. Inside the lantern, a cylindrical, golden-yellow object, possibly a candle or lamp, is centrally positioned at the base. The lantern has a tall, pyramidal, vented top with evenly spaced round holes for ventilation. Attached to the apex of the top is a large, circular metal handle, shown in a slightly off-center position. The entire object is set against a plain, beige background, and the artist’s signature “Son Alexander Del. 1850” is written in small letters near the bottom right corner of the composition.
title: Lantern
cluster: #16 — Lighting Devices: Lamps, Lanterns, and Candleholders
